Santiago Vega and I collaborated daily during his tenure at FinTech Innovators Inc., where he led embedded systems development for real-time financial transaction platforms. His role required balancing hardware constraints with stringent reliability demands, and he consistently delivered solutions that aligned with both technical and business goals.  

Santiago’s daily work centered on optimizing embedded Linux kernels for low-latency performance, often refining firmware to reduce power consumption by 15-20% in edge devices. He frequently used C/C++ to debug complex interactions between hardware peripherals and custom RTOS kernels, ensuring stability under high-throughput scenarios. Python scripts he developed automated testing workflows, cutting regression cycle times by nearly a third. His REST API designs for device management systems were clean and scalable, enabling seamless integration across distributed systems.  

One standout project involved rearchitecting a legacy IoT protocol stack to support MQTT over CoAP, which improved device communication reliability by 35% in edge networks. Another was his work on a firmware update mechanism that slashed deployment errors by 40%, leveraging secure boot and over-the-air signing. Santiago’s ability to bridge hardware-software gaps was critical during a hardware revision, where he identified a timing mismatch that caused intermittent failures in sensor arrays.  

Santiago is a meticulous problem-solver with a knack for simplifying complex systems. His work ethic and technical depth make him a strong candidate for roles requiring precision and innovation in embedded systems.
